findings.title: Health-import wizard: 'skip for now' on the last remaining item loops back to the same item
findings.user_impact: The user pressed 'דלג כרגע' on the sleep-schedule confirmation three times and received the identical screen back each time; the only escape was 'דלג על שאר האישורים'.
deterministic_facts: Events 66/75/84: three consecutive health:skip_item presses on the sleep_schedule item.
After each press the flow completed and immediately restarted at step __health_edit_sleep_schedule__ (flow.started events 71, 80, 89 — all with flow_after.step __health_edit_sleep_schedule__).
The re-rendered question text was byte-identical each time (renders 63/72/81).
Earlier in the same wizard (event 37), skip_item on sleep DID advance — to avg_steps — while other unconfirmed items remained.
explicit_assumptions: The loop occurs specifically when the skipped item is the only unconfirmed item left: 'skip for now' re-queues it as the next pending item instead of ending the wizard.

evidence_references.note: first of the three identical skip loops

findings.suspected_root_cause: skip_item marks the item 'ask later' and recomputes the next unconfirmed item, which is the same item when nothing else remains; there is no terminal branch for 'all remaining items skipped'.
findings.proposed_regression: Harness journey: drive the wizard to a single remaining item, press health:skip_item, assert the flow terminates (wizard summary rendered) instead of restarting at the same step.

approval_record.approved_scope: Root-cause fix of the GENERIC wizard skip/progression behavior (not only the sleep item), with generic + incident-specific regression coverage

findings.title: Stale/duplicate control presses are dropped with no visible acknowledgement
findings.user_impact: Twice the user tapped a button and — as far as the recorded conversation shows — nothing happened at all, which reads as the bot hanging.
deterministic_facts: Event 275 (in_1bc6bde7ca064f3a): pressing the step-1 wizard button after the wizard had advanced produced routing.decided and then zero further events — no render, no state change.
Event 601 (in_558c5fea44be4afc): a second approve_meal press after the meal was saved produced zero further events.
Both interactions are the two interaction_no_output signals; the refusals themselves were CORRECT (no double-save, no wizard regression).
explicit_assumptions: The user perceived silence. A Telegram callback toast (query.answer) may have been shown but is not instrumented, so the recorded experience is silence.
missing_information: Whether query.answer produced any visible toast on these two refusal paths.
findings.suspected_root_cause: The identity/duplicate gates (B2/B5 family) return early on refusal without sending any user-visible acknowledgement.
findings.proposed_regression: Harness journey: press a stale wizard control and a duplicate approve control; assert a delivered acknowledgement render (or recorded callback answer) exists in the trace.

approval_record.approved_scope: CONDITIONAL: reproduce first; preserve stale/duplicate rejection and idempotency; add a short user-visible acknowledgement instead of silence; coordinate with F-03
approval_record.notes: Operator requires reproduction before treating as fact

findings.title: Refusal decisions and callback ACKs are invisible to the trace
findings.user_impact: A correct silent refusal is indistinguishable from a hang in the canonical trace, which will repeatedly waste review time.
deterministic_facts: In both no-output interactions (events 267-275, 590-601) the trace ends after routing.decided: the gate refusal emitted no decision.* event.
query.answer / answer_callback_query is not an instrumented delivery boundary anywhere in the O1-O10 event stream (no ACK events exist in this window).
explicit_assumptions: Any control-refusal path (not only these two gates) likely shares the gap.
findings.suspected_root_cause: The gates predate a 'refusal is a decision' convention: nothing emits decision.finalized(outcome=refused, reason=stale_control|duplicate), and ACK toasts bypass the egress instrumentation.
findings.proposed_regression: Trace assertion: a refused control press yields decision.finalized outcome=refused with a machine-readable reason in the same interaction.

approval_record.approved_scope: Instrument intentional callback refusals (stale/duplicate) and callback toast acknowledgements so they are distinguishable from hangs and delivery failures

findings.title: Goal-weight typo guard suggests a nonsensical example value
findings.user_impact: A 58 kg user aiming at 48 kg was told to either confirm or write another goal, e.g. 83 — a 25 kg GAIN example that undermines trust in the guard.
deterministic_facts: Event 348: the guard render for input 48 (current weight 58) ends with the example value 83.
explicit_assumptions: The example value is hardcoded (likely from a different authoring context) instead of derived from the user's current weight.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Static example text in the goal-weight sanity-check template.
findings.proposed_regression: Unit test: the guard message example value is within a plausible band of the user's current weight.

approval_record.approved_scope: Fix underlying formatting/derivation rule + focused regression

findings.title: Partial-estimate goal card renders a dangling empty 'missing items' header
findings.user_impact: The goal card promises a list of missing items after a colon and shows nothing, looking broken.
deterministic_facts: Event 370: the daily-goal render contains the missing-items header followed directly by the next warning block — zero items.
explicit_assumptions: The missing-items collection was empty but the header renders unconditionally.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Header rendered before checking the emptiness of the missing-details list.
findings.proposed_regression: Unit test: partial-estimate goal card with no missing items renders no dangling header.

approval_record.approved_scope: Fix underlying formatting rule + focused regression

findings.title: Multiple live plan-center cards run parallel wizard instances with version churn
findings.user_impact: Three separate messages (1617/1619/1621) all became the plan center with live generate buttons; pressing generate on one silently invalidated the wizard buttons on another (v39 to v40), producing the dead press of F-02 and a confusing multi-card state.
deterministic_facts: Messages 1617, 1619 and 1621 each rendered the plan center with planv2:generate buttons during the session.
Events 244 and 256: planv2:generate:workout pressed on two different messages within a minute; the second regenerated the wizard with token v40 while message 1621 still displayed v39 buttons.
Event 275: the subsequent v39 press was refused with no output (see F-02).
explicit_assumptions: The user did not realize older cards stay interactive but stale; the wizard state is global while cards are per-message.
missing_information: Whether superseding is intended UX for plan-center cards (vs. decommissioning old cards visually).
findings.suspected_root_cause: Plan-center renders are per-message but wizard/selection state is singleton; regeneration bumps the version token without editing superseded cards to a non-interactive state.
findings.proposed_regression: Harness journey: render plan center twice, generate on the newer card, assert the older card is edited to a superseded state or its press yields an explicit refusal message.

approval_record.approved_scope: Reproduction + root-cause investigation; implement ONLY if the parallel authoritative-card/stale-version interaction is confirmed; no broad navigation redesign
approval_record.notes: Stop and report if scope proves broader

findings.title: Workout menu claims today's workout is already completed on the user's first day
findings.user_impact: A brand-new user (onboarded 80 minutes earlier, zero in-bot workout activity) opened the workout menu and was told today's workout is already completed.
deterministic_facts: Event 1 of the database is this user's /start earlier the same session; no workout set/session events exist anywhere in the window.
Event 623: the workout menu render states the day's workout is already completed.
explicit_assumptions: The completion flag may derive legitimately from the Apple Health import (1,378 records through 2026-07-15, possibly including a workout today) — but the message gives no attribution, so it reads as false state.
missing_information: Whether an imported Health workout for 2026-07-15 exists and is the source of the completion flag.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Workout-completion state presented without provenance; if import-sourced, the message should attribute it to the imported health data.
findings.proposed_regression: Unit test: workout menu on a day whose only completion evidence is imported attributes the completion to the import in the message.

findings.title: A soft food preference is presented as a hard prohibition in the profile
findings.user_impact: The user explicitly chose the softest option (prefer to avoid) for fruit; the profile screen lists it under hard dietary prohibitions, misrepresenting what they said.
deterministic_facts: Event 224: the preference-level button was chosen (label: prefer to avoid).
Event 227: storage correctly recorded allergies=none (the classification IS distinguished internally).
Event 436: the profile render lists fruit under the dietary-prohibitions label.
explicit_assumptions: Menu-generation severity may also treat preference as prohibition (not proven here — the day's menus simply contained no fruit).
missing_information: Which fact the profile renderer reads and whether downstream menu constraints honor the preference/allergy distinction.
findings.suspected_root_cause: The profile renderer labels the diet_restrictions fact as prohibitions regardless of the stored classification level.
findings.proposed_regression: Unit test: a preference-classified restriction renders under a preference label, not under prohibitions.

approval_record.approved_scope: Fix underlying classification/labeling rule + focused regression

findings.title: Protein overshoot is shown as a negative remainder in the save summary
findings.user_impact: After the second meal the save summary showed a remaining protein of minus five grams, while the status screen correctly phrases the same state as an overshoot — inconsistent, and the raw negative looks like a bug.
deterministic_facts: Event 598: save-summary render contains the raw negative remaining-protein value.
The subsequent status render phrases the same state as an overshoot of five grams.
explicit_assumptions: The save-summary path lacks the overshoot phrasing the status path already has.
findings.suspected_root_cause: Two renderers format remaining protein independently; only one clamps and rephrases negatives.
findings.proposed_regression: Unit test: overshoot renders the same phrasing in the save summary as in the status screen.

approval_record.approved_scope: Fix underlying formatting rule + focused regression
